title: Why Tourists Love Foreign Supermarkets
paragraphs: When people travel abroad, they usually plan to visit famous museums, historic buildings and popular restaurants. Increasingly, however, many travelers are adding a far more ordinary destination to their list: the local supermarket.

This trend, sometimes known as "supermarket tourism" or "grocery store tourism," has been growing in recent years, particularly in Asia but also in Europe and North America. According to the hotel company Hilton's 2026 Trends Report, which was based on a survey of more than 14,000 travelers in 14 countries, 77% of travelers say they enjoy visiting grocery stores abroad. In addition, almost half said they cook their own meals while traveling.

So why do so many people enjoy shopping for groceries on holiday? For many, it is a way of seeing how local people really live. As one traveler from Malaysia explained to a newspaper, supermarkets show "what locals actually eat and drink every day," which she finds more interesting than souvenir shops. Supermarkets also allow visitors to discover unfamiliar products, compare prices with those at home and buy affordable gifts for friends and family.
Social media has also played an important role. Many travelers save videos on platforms such as TikTok showing "viral" products to look for, from snacks to cosmetics.

Some stores have started responding to the trend. In Thailand, for example, larger outlets of the supermarket chain Big C have a section for tourists listing the "top 10 Thai items to buy," including herbal inhalers, beauty products and rice snacks. Meanwhile, in Malaysia, the supermarket chain Jaya Grocer has worked with the national tourism organization to display products made by local companies. According to the company, "Retail has become an important part of the overall tourism experience."

Convenience stores have also become attractions. One Malaysian traveler described 7-Eleven stores in Thailand as being "like paradise," with popular products such as coconut rolls and instant Thai tea. However, popularity can also cause problems. When a Lawson store in Fujikawaguchiko became famous online for its view of Mount Fuji, the crowds of tourists became so large that security staff had to be brought in.
